subtopic: Fused kernels / Benefits and boundary conditions
learningObjective: Distinguish real benefits and non-benefits of kernel fusion for transformer building blocks.
stem: Select all correct statements about kernel fusion in transformer inference. (Choose all that apply.)

options.text: Kernel fusion always improves latency because it eliminates all HBM traffic between the fused ops; there is no configuration in which fusion hurts performance.
Aggressive fusion can hurt occupancy by inflating per-thread register footprint; when register pressure spills to local memory, the fused kernel may be slower than the un-fused version.
Fusion primarily reduces HBM roundtrips of intermediate tensors and amortizes kernel-launch overhead; the FLOP count of the fused operations is unchanged.

Producer-consumer fusion (e.g., pointwise ops on the output of a GEMM) is straightforward, but fusing across a reduction boundary (e.g., across softmax) requires restructuring the tiling and typically only pays off under specific tile-size constraints.

explanation: Options B, C, D are correct; option A is incorrect. A (Wrong): fusion has real costs; not universally beneficial. B (Correct): register pressure can undo the gains. C (Correct): fusion reduces HBM traffic and launch overhead. D (Correct): reduction-boundary fusion is hard and conditional.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: fusion has real costs; not universally beneficial.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: register pressure can undo the gains.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: fusion reduces HBM traffic and launch overhead.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: reduction-boundary fusion is hard and conditional.

assumptions: 'Fusion' means combining multiple logical ops into a single kernel launch.
GPU with register file and SMEM as the on-chip staging levels.
nonImplications: Does not imply un-fused kernels are ever better on typical shapes; when register pressure is fine, fusion wins.
Does not imply fusion decisions are static; auto-tuners typically evaluate multiple fusion configurations.
